question: What is the term for when the body takes absorbed nutrients and builds them into body tissues?
explanation: Assimilation is how the body uses absorbed nutrients to build and repair cell structures. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h1)

question: Why is simply eating food (ingestion) not enough to keep body cells healthy?

options.A: Eaten food turns straight into body fat
options.B: Cells can only take in raw solid food
options.C: Food must be broken down and absorbed to reach cells
options.D: The stomach ruins all vitamins right away

explanation: Food particles are too large to enter cells until digestion breaks them down and absorption brings them into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h1)

question: When dietary proteins are completely digested, what do they break down into?
explanation: Proteins are broken down into amino acids so the intestines can easily absorb them. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h2)

question: A patient has a blockage in their intestinal lymphatic vessels. Which nutrient absorption will be most affected?
explanation: Long-chain fats travel through the lymphatic system rather than the regular blood vessels. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h2)

question: Inside the cell, where does the breakdown of fatty acids for energy mostly happen?
explanation: Fatty acids go into the mitochondria, which are the powerhouses of the cell, to produce energy. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h3)

question: What decides whether the body breaks down nutrients or builds them into stores?

options.A: The time of day the food was eaten
options.B: The pH level of the blood
options.C: How much water was drunk that day
options.D: The current energy needs of the cell

explanation: Cells switch between storing energy and burning it based on what their immediate ATP needs are. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h3)

question: What is the main job of B-complex vitamins in cell metabolism?

options.A: Acting as coenzymes to help produce energy
options.D: Carrying oxygen straight to the muscles

explanation: B vitamins work as coenzymes that help chemical reactions release energy in the body. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h4)

question: What happens when a person takes in more water-soluble vitamins than they need?

options.A: Cell energy shoots up very high
options.B: They are stored in body fat
options.C: The kidneys filter them out in the urine

explanation: Water-soluble vitamins are not stored in large amounts, so extra amounts are passed out through the kidneys. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h4)

question: Where does the body mostly store extra glucose as glycogen?
explanation: The liver and muscles keep stores of glycogen ready to supply quick energy when needed. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h5)

question: When does the body start turning extra nutrients into fat (lipogenesis)?

options.A: When glycogen storage is completely full
options.B: During the first hour of heavy exercise
options.C: Right after eating any dietary fat
options.D: When blood sugar drops very low

explanation: The body stores extra energy as glycogen first, and only makes fat once those glycogen spots are full. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h5)

question: Which type of iron found in food is absorbed best by the human gut?
explanation: Heme iron comes from animal foods and is absorbed much easier than iron from plants. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h6)

question: How do phytates in plant foods affect mineral absorption in the gut?

options.A: They turn water-soluble vitamins into fat-soluble ones
options.B: They bind to minerals and stop them from being absorbed
options.D: They kill bad bacteria in the gut

explanation: Phytates attach to minerals like iron and zinc, making it hard for the gut to absorb them. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h6)

question: What is the main sign that helps tell kwashiorkor apart from marasmus?
explanation: Kwashiorkor is caused by a severe lack of protein, leading to low blood protein and noticeable fluid swelling. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h7)

question: A patient with long-term body inflammation develops anemia even though their iron intake is normal. Why does this happen?

options.A: Liver glycogen turns iron into fat
options.B: Red blood cells get destroyed in the stomach
options.C: The kidneys flush out all iron instantly
options.D: Inflammation traps iron so the body cannot use it

explanation: Long-term inflammation causes the body to lock up its iron stores, keeping it away from where new red blood cells are made. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h7)

question: Which blood test do nurses commonly check to assess a patient's protein levels and nutrition?
explanation: Serum albumin is a standard blood test used to check protein levels and nutritional health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h8)

question: A nurse cares for a patient with pancreatic enzyme problems. What action helps them digest food better?

options.A: Stopping all water intake to avoid fluid overload
options.B: Giving a diet of only clear liquids
options.C: Giving prescribed pancreatic enzyme pills with meals

explanation: Taking prescribed pancreatic enzymes helps make up for what the pancreas cannot make, allowing proper food digestion. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h8)
